title: Annotatio IV §.XXIII: Body existed psychikōs and pneumatikōs; last Adam life-giving spirit; SPIRITUALLY participable
pass_a_gloss: The most subtle Author adds in Num. 4 p. 330: The Lord’s Body viewed in itself has not existed in one mode only: not psychikōs only, but also pneumatikōs: for the last Adam (i.e. Christ) was made into a life-giving spirit, 1 Cor. 15:45. What hinders that, as it exists in itself, so also it be participated by us? SPIRITUALLY it can without all doubt be participated; and so our participation will stand firm enough for us — nay it will be the truest and most principal. But whether it can now be participated Naturally, especially by eating and drinking — whose condition (if it has human nature for its Object) abhors farthest from Nature itself — we know many other obstacles are set, which we do not now delay to list; for removing them not even Rome itself suffices.
pass_b_english: Wren (n. 4 p. 330): the Lord’s body in itself existed not in one mode only — not psychically alone but also pneumatically. The last Adam (Christ) was made a life-giving spirit (1 Cor. 15:45).

As it exists in itself, so it can be participated: SPIRITUALLY without doubt — our truest and chief participation. Natural eating and drinking of human nature as object abhors farthest from nature; other obstacles Rome itself cannot remove.
source_text: Addit Auctor subtilissimus Num. 4. p. 330. Corpus Domini in se spectatum, non unô modô exstitisse: Non psychikōs solùm, sed & pneumatikōs etiam: Factus est enim novissimus Adam (h.e. Christus) in spiritum vivificantem 1. Cor. 15. 45. Ecquid impedit, quin, ut existit in se, ita & participetur à nobis? SPIRITUALITER procul omni dubio participari potest; Atque ita satis constabit nobis participatio nostra, sed & verissima ea & principalissima erit. Naturaliter verò ne participari jam possit præfertim per manducationem & bibitionem; Quarum conditio (si humanam naturam pro Objecto suo, habeat) ab ipsâ Naturâ longissimè abhorret. Novimus alios plures obices poni, quibus recensendis nunc non moramur, amovendis quidem ne ipsa Roma sufficit.
